questions.q: Per this lesson's recommended sequence, what should an architect check first when a query against an LDV-scale object is slow?
options: Whether Salesforce Support can enable divisions immediately
Whether the object should be converted to a Big Object
Whether the filter is built against an indexed field, before evaluating selectivity or escalating to Support
Whether the record should simply be deleted
questions.explain: The sequence starts with confirming the filter targets an indexed field, then checks selectivity, and only escalates to custom indexes, skinny tables, or divisions after those self-service steps are exhausted.

questions.q: What does a division do that a WHERE-clause filter on an ordinary field doesn't?
options: It hides records from users who lack permission to see them
It automatically indexes every field on the object
It converts the object into a skinny table
It lets the platform pre-scope an entire partition of data (e.g., using WITH in SOSL) before other filtering runs, rather than filtering it out row by row
questions.explain: Division scoping (especially via SOSL's WITH clause) lets the platform exclude an entire division's worth of data up front, which is generally faster than an equivalent WHERE condition evaluated against every row.

questions.q: Which of these is a real constraint on Salesforce divisions, per this lesson?
options: Divisions cannot be disabled once enabled, making it a one-way architectural decision
Divisions can be freely toggled on and off at any time
Divisions automatically restrict record visibility, replacing the need for a sharing model
Any org can self-enable divisions through a Setup checkbox regardless of size
questions.explain: Divisions are enabled by Salesforce Support and, once enabled, cannot be disabled — an architect has to be confident in the decision before recommending it, since there's no undo.

questions.q: Why are divisions explicitly NOT described as a security or visibility control in this lesson?
options: Because divisions don't actually exist as a real Salesforce feature
Because divisions partition data for performance scoping only — hiding records from unauthorized users is still the job of the sharing model, not the division assignment
Because divisions automatically encrypt all record data
Because divisions only apply to custom objects, never to objects with sharing rules
questions.explain: A division's purpose is to speed up searches, reports, and queries by pre-scoping an object's total row set — it is not a substitute for the org's sharing model, which remains responsible for actual record-level access control.

questions.q: A slow report's filter is already selective and backed by a standard index, but the object's standard/custom field join is still the main bottleneck. Which lever from this chapter most directly addresses that specific cause?
options: Requesting divisions
Switching the report to a dashboard
A skinny table
Disabling the Recycle Bin
questions.explain: A skinny table specifically avoids the standard/custom field join by combining frequently-used fields into one structure — it directly addresses a join bottleneck, which indexing and selectivity fixes (aimed at filtering) and divisions (aimed at pre-scoping the whole object) don't.
